title: Biotechnology and its Applications
seo_title: Biotechnology and its Applications Class 12 Biology Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 10)
standard_code: Class 12 Biology, Chapter 10: Biotechnology and its Applications
standard_text: Application of biotechnology in health and agriculture: genetically modified organisms – Bt crops; transgenic animals; biosafety issues, biopiracy and patents.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 12 Biology worksheets for NCERT Chapter 10 Biotechnology and its Applications: Bt crops, RNA interference, genetically engineered insulin, gene therapy, molecular diagnosis, transgenic animals, biosafety, patents and biopiracy. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Bt crops make their own insect-killing protein.
key_sub: Recombinant DNA gives insulin, vaccines and gene therapy.
body_html:
How to think about it

In agriculture, Bt cotton carries cry genes from Bacillus thuringiensis whose protoxin becomes active in the alkaline gut of insect larvae. RNA interference protects tobacco from nematodes. Golden rice is rich in vitamin A. In medicine, E. coli makes human insulin (A and B chains joined by disulphide bonds), gene therapy treated ADA deficiency, and PCR and ELISA allow early diagnosis.

Transgenic animals are used to study diseases and make products such as α-lactalbumin-rich milk (Rosie the cow). In India GEAC decides on the safety of GM research. Patents and biopiracy raise questions about the use of a nation's bio-resources.

Example

Bt toxin gene for bollworms?

cry

Answer: cryIAc

Example

First gene therapy?

1990

Answer: ADA deficiency

Common mistakes

  • Saying the Bt toxin kills the bacterium that makes it.
  • Calling a cloned animal transgenic.
  • Thinking insulin is made as one chain in E. coli.

Silencing a specific mRNA with complementary double-stranded RNA, used to protect tobacco roots from nematodes.

items.q: Why is early detection of disease by PCR useful?
